dedupe_keys.name: eia u s energy atlas and energy maps geospatial layers for us energy infrastructure resources and disruptions

description: The US Energy Information Administration publishes its maps on eia.gov/maps and points users to the U.S. Energy Atlas, its interface for web map applications and a geospatial data catalogue. The maps page lists map details and data for federal lands, NGL and natural gas market hubs, oil and gas refining and processing, oil and gas wells, pipelines and electric transmission, power plants, energy resources, storage, and waterborne transport including petroleum ports and LNG terminals. It also links an energy disruptions map that overlays energy infrastructure on real-time storm tracking, historical disruption reports and a flood vulnerability assessment map combining FEMA flood hazard with infrastructure layers, plus static PDF, PNG and JPG maps. On the day of cataloguing the Atlas search API listed 76 items, mostly tight oil and shale gas play feature services, natural gas storage regions and PADD boundaries, with reference layers such as weather warnings, hurricanes, wildfires and the US wind turbine database. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): Public domain (EIA: public domain and use of EIA content). Access is free of charge. Coverage is the United States. Caveats: the Atlas is a JavaScript application that could not be read as text, the infrastructure layers listed on the maps page did not appear in the Atlas search results, and some static maps are old. Simulation uses are US energy infrastructure layers for hazard overlay and disruption studies. Related records: data-hifld-open covers the federal infrastructure layers.
